newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: El Salvador still losing coffee output to broca.
newsitem.headline: El Salvador still losing coffee output to broca.

text.p: El Salvador loses around 100,000 quintals (100 lb or 46 kg) bags of coffee each cycle to broca, a technical official from the Salvadoran Foundation for Coffee Investigations (Procafe) said Monday.
"Easily, the country can lose around 100,000 quintals of coffee (per cycle) which represents around $14 million," Manuel Vega, the manager of Procafe's plant protection unit told Reuters.
Broca is the notorious berry borer that reduces bean quality and weight and is found in most coffee producing countries in the world and it is one of the most troublesome pests.
Vega said broca has been detected in 80 percent, or 132,000 hectares, of the 169,000 hectares planted with the beans in the tiny central American country.
But he said El Salvador had managed to put the brakes on the spreading of the disease since control measures were started in 1990.
Vega said the on-going broca control measures will in three years' time mean that only a minimal surface area of coffee will still have the berry borer.
